answer: A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 126 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The yarrow detector writes to vault, and delta shows every merge. Submissions that land within 92 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 31 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
